methodology.description: LiteLLM dedup measurement on real SWE-bench Lite instances

arms.without_dedup: Same proxy with TOOLRECALL_DEDUP_DISABLED=1 (hook passes through)

methodology.workload_description: 8-turn agent debugging conversation constructed from real SWE-bench instances. Each turn simulates a phase of an agent's workflow: read problem, read source files, re-read to trace flow, propose fix, re-read to verify, apply patch, re-read post-fix, run tests. File content at base_commit fetched from GitHub raw. 200-line truncated blocks (per SWE-bench convention).
methodology.token_counting: usage.prompt_tokens from OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions response. This is the provider-billed prompt token count. Cost estimate at $0.15/M input tokens.
methodology.verification: Separate OpenRouter API keys per arm. Per-key billed spend visible on https://openrouter.ai/dashboard — cross-verifies reported token counts.
caveats: Measures token savings, not task success rate. Opt-in design, protected_tail=2.
Hook only fires on /v1/chat/completions (litellm#27518 — /v1/messages not covered).
Request-level dedup, different from LiteLLM's response caching.
methodology.reproduce:
pip install litellm toolrecall datasets
python3 measure_swebench.py --json > result.json
MEASURE_INSTANCES=10 MEASURE_MAX_TURNS=8 MEASURE_MODEL=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash

note: Accumulating agent loop: turn N = single request carrying turns 1..N. 10 SWE-bench Lite instances x 8 turns = 80 requests/arm. Model deepseek-v4-flash via LiteLLM proxy.
